projection.units: Original archive coordinates flagged as km, with mesh volume-equivalent diameter 55.9999995 km and archive-declared diameter 56 km. The unchanged coordinates are uniformly rescaled by 0.87500000787523258 km per source unit to the explicitly selected published volume-equivalent diameter 49 km (Ďurech et al. (2011), Icarus 214, 652–670); the original archive diameter is not the adopted physical scale.

inputs.coverage: Convex light-curve reconstruction, 49 ± 5 km volume-equivalent diameter. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative. The pole(79,−35) is preferred by both IRAS thermal fits and the2004 occultation negative chord. Delbo and Tanga2009 obtain a volume-equivalent thermal size range55–57 km, represented in DAMIT as56±1 km. The later Ďurech2011 Table3 fits the same pole family to five occultation chords at49±5 km. This explicit occultation volume scale is transferred uniformly to the archived shape; the distinct thermal estimate is retained as a comparison rather than silently averaged.
